newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jagoda says 97 unemployment to exceed gov forecast.
newsitem.headline: Jagoda says 97 unemployment to exceed gov forecast.

text.p: Federal Labour Office President Bernhard Jagoda said on Friday he could no longer endorse the government's official forecast of 3.95 million average unemployment in 1997.
"I believe the target figure of 3.95 million jobless for 1997 is no longer attainable," Jagoda told a news conference.

Another Labour Office official told the same news conference that based on data from the first five months of the year, and an assumption of 2.25 percent economic growth, average unemployment could go as high as 4.29 million.
The government's official forecast is for 1997 GDP growth of 2.5 percent, but most private sector economists are sceptical it will be reached.
"Even our most optimistic forecasts indicate a figure of 4.23 million," said the second official, Gerhard Kleinhenz, head

Economists said the rise in May showed the German economy wasn't recovering as fast as previously thought, endangering the government's drive to narrow its budget deficit and qualify for European monetary union.

"This is bad news for (Finance Minister Theo) Waigel," said Ulrich Beckmann, a senior economist at Deutsche Bank Research in Frankfurt. "These figures are disappointing compared with our forecast... An increase of 56,000 does not fit into our growth scenario for the economy."
Adrian Owens at Julius Bear Investments in Frankfurt also said the May figures were a setback for the economy, but did not rule improvement this year.
"I think that in a broader context we are seeing a stabilisation and will see that increasingly in the latter part of the year," he said.
